prompt.context: Federal Motors (FM) is the biggest US producer of passenger cars and trucks. It currently has 5 different brands: Maddilac (luxury), Frenchroller (mass market), Muick (between luxury and mass market), Rontiac (sport cars), and Lammer (heavy cars, trucks and regular cars). FM sells cars across the world — 60% of sales in the US, 20% in China, and 20% in other countries (Russia, India, Brazil). All brands are sold in all countries, but the sales structure and prices differ by country. FM desperately wants to increase profits and the CEO has approached us to help.
prompt.question: What is driving FM's profitability problem, and what recommendations would you make to increase profits?

clarifying_info.q: Do we have data on sales volumes and prices by brand?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — we have sales structure data for North America only (will be shared as Exhibit 1).
Yes — cost structure per vehicle will be shared as Exhibit 2.

clarifying_info.q: Do we have any information on customers?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — customer loyalty and satisfaction data for North America will be shared as Exhibit 3, and China brand data as Exhibit 4.
We do not have any information on competitors.
The market is stable and we do not have any forecasts for the future.

exhibits.title: Sales Structure North America
exhibits.shows: Two bar charts: (1) number of thousands of vehicles sold per brand in North America; (2) average price per vehicle by brand in North America (in thousands of dollars).
exhibits.data: Maddillac: 550K units at $50K; Frenchroller: 1,950K units at $30K; Muik: 350K units at $35K; Rontiac: 200K units at $27K; Lammer: 150K units at $60K

exhibits.title: Cost Structure Per Vehicle
exhibits.shows: A table of per-vehicle costs (in thousands of dollars) broken down by cost category for each brand.
exhibits.data: Maddillac — Car:30, Marketing:10, Transportation:2, Warehouse:1, SG&A:2 (Total:45); Frenchroller — Car:20, Marketing:3, Transportation:2, Warehouse:1, SG&A:2 (Total:28); Muik — Car:27, Marketing:4, Transportation:2, Warehouse:1, SG&A:2 (Total:36); Rontiac — Car:22, Marketing:4, Transportation:2, Warehouse:1, SG&A:2 (Total:31); Lammer — Car:45, Marketing:15, Transportation:3, Warehouse:2, SG&A:3 (Total:68)

exhibits.title: Client Loyalty and Satisfaction — North America
exhibits.shows: Two bar charts showing (1) clients' loyalty (% who stick with the brand after first purchase) and (2) clients' satisfaction (% satisfied with the car) by brand in North America.
exhibits.data: Loyalty — Maddillac:87%, Frenchroller:80%, Muik:45%, Rontiac:35%, Lammer:20%; Satisfaction — Maddillac:90%, Frenchroller:85%, Muik:50%, Rontiac:37%, Lammer:25%

exhibits.title: Revenue and Loyalty by Brand — China
exhibits.shows: Two bar charts showing (1) revenue share by brand and (2) loyalty by brand in China. Only three brands appear: Maddillac, Frenchroller, and Muik.
exhibits.data: Revenue share in China: Muik dominates (~70%), followed by Frenchroller (~20%) and Maddillac (~10%). Loyalty in China: Muik has the highest loyalty (~90%), Frenchroller and Maddillac lower.

framework: Clarify problem scope: profitability = revenue minus costs; need to analyze by brand
Assess revenue structure: units sold × price per brand in North America
Assess cost structure: per-vehicle costs by brand and category
Calculate profit per vehicle and total profit by brand
Identify unprofitable brands; assess whether to reprice or discontinue
Check customer loyalty and satisfaction as a signal of brand health
Check performance in other key markets (China) before making discontinuation decisions
Formulate recommendation: reprice or close unprofitable brands; protect strategically important ones

questions.prompt: What is the total revenue of Federal Motors in North America, and what is the revenue contribution of each brand?
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply units sold by average price for each brand and sum. Should notice that Frenchroller and Maddillac together drive roughly 75% of revenue. Should flag that having five brands could be a driver of overhead costs.

math.setup: Revenue per brand = Units sold (thousands) × Average price ($K). Total revenue = sum across all brands.
math.answer: Total North America revenue ≈ $112.65B. Frenchroller (~52%) and Maddillac (~24%) together account for ~76% of revenue.

questions.prompt: How much does it cost to manufacture and sell each vehicle by brand? Which brands are profitable and which are losing money?
questions.guidance: Candidate should sum all cost components per vehicle for each brand, then compare to price. Should identify Muik, Rontiac, and Lammer as loss-making. Should note Rontiac and Lammer have particularly poor margins. Should consider whether to raise prices, cut costs, or abandon unprofitable brands.

math.setup: Profit per vehicle = Price − Total cost per vehicle. Total cost = Car + Marketing + Transportation + Warehouse + SG&A.
steps: Rontiac: $27K − (22+4+2+1+2)=$31K → Loss −$4K, margin −11% (Note: price listed as $27K vs total cost $31K)
Lammer: $60K − (45+15+3+2+3)=$68K → Loss −$8K, margin −30% (Note: price listed as $60K vs total cost $68K)
math.answer: Maddillac and Frenchroller are profitable. Muik, Rontiac, and Lammer are all losing money. Lammer has the worst margin at −30%.

questions.prompt: What does the customer loyalty and satisfaction data tell us about each brand? What options do we have for the losing brands?
questions.guidance: Strong answer: Rontiac and Lammer have both low loyalty and low satisfaction — poor candidates for turnaround. Muik has middling loyalty/satisfaction but is not as dire. Options: raise prices (if demand is inelastic), reduce costs (told it is not possible), or discontinue the brand. Candidate should probe each option and weigh trade-offs.

questions.prompt: Before recommending to close Muik, what additional considerations should we check? (China market)
questions.guidance: Candidate should consider international exposure. In China, Muik is the dominant brand by revenue (~70% share) and has very high loyalty. Closing Muik in the US could damage brand perception in China and significantly hurt FM's Chinese revenue. Therefore Muik should not be closed — instead FM should raise prices in the US to eliminate the per-vehicle loss.

brainstorming.prompt: What options does FM have for brands that are losing money?

categories.name: Pricing
ideas: Raise prices for loss-making brands (Muik, Rontiac, Lammer) to cover costs
Use tiered pricing or regional pricing to extract more value in markets with inelastic demand

categories.name: Cost reduction
ideas: Reduce manufacturing costs through process improvements or supplier renegotiation
Consolidate platforms/components across brands to achieve scale economies
Reduce marketing spend for lower-priority brands
Close inefficient warehousing or logistics nodes

categories.name: Brand discontinuation
ideas: Exit Rontiac and Lammer brands given low loyalty, low satisfaction, and persistent losses
Phase out gradually vs. immediate closure to manage customer impact

categories.name: Portfolio restructuring
ideas: Consolidate Muik, Rontiac, Lammer into fewer brands to reduce overhead
Reposition Muik as a premium offering to justify higher prices
License or divest underperforming brands to third parties

categories.name: Market considerations
ideas: Maintain Muik globally because it is strategically critical in China
Assess whether Rontiac or Lammer have strong performance in other markets before closing
Focus investment on Maddillac and Frenchroller which drive 75%+ of revenue

recommendation: Close Rontiac and Lammer brands: both are deeply unprofitable (−11% and −30% margins) and have the lowest customer loyalty and satisfaction in North America, with no indication of strategic value in other markets.

Raise prices for Muik in the US to eliminate the per-vehicle loss: do NOT close Muik because it is the dominant brand in China (~70% revenue share, highest loyalty), and closing it in the US would risk damaging the brand globally.
Focus investment on Maddillac and Frenchroller, which together account for ~76% of North American revenue and are both profitable.
risks: Closing Rontiac and Lammer may impact employees, dealers, and supply chain partners — requires careful wind-down planning.
Raising Muik prices in the US may further reduce already-moderate customer loyalty/satisfaction domestically.
Simplifying to fewer brands reduces portfolio breadth and may cede market segments to competitors.
next_steps: Analyze profitability and customer data for Rontiac and Lammer in other international markets before finalizing closure.
Model the price elasticity of Muik in the US to determine the optimal price increase.
Develop a dealer transition and brand exit plan for Rontiac and Lammer.
Assess synergy opportunities from consolidating manufacturing and marketing across fewer brands.
